case_law.Court / citation: N.D. Cal. No. 5:18-cv-07182; 9th Cir. (unpublished memo); 9th Cir. No. 24-5538
case_law.Date(s): Feb. 18, 2022 (9th Cir. memo, preliminary injunction); July 22, 2024 (findings: US$597,000 damages, permanent injunction); Aug. 15, 2024 (judgment entered); Dec. 10, 2025 (9th Cir. No. 24-5538 dismissed on stipulated voluntary dismissal); Dec. 15, 2025 (satisfaction of judgment)
case_law.Holding / status: Licensor may combine AGPL with Commons Clause; AGPL §7/§10 bar further restrictions only by licensees ("you"), so licensees cannot strip licensor-imposed terms. Non-precedential; no appellate merits ruling on §7
case_law.Why it matters: Do not assume "AGPL + rider" can be cleaned to plain AGPL

case_law.Case: Software Freedom Conservancy v. Vizio, Inc.
case_law.Court / citation: Cal. Super. Ct., Orange County, No. 30-2021-01226723-CU-BC-CJC
case_law.Date(s): Dec. 23, 2025 (minute order); trial reportedly began Aug. 10, 2026
case_law.Holding / status: Pretrial order: GPLv2/LGPLv2.1 require source that can be obtained and modified (incl. installation scripts), but not enabling reinstallation such that the device continues to function properly. Third-party-beneficiary enforcement by purchasers remains at issue. No post-trial judgment found
case_law.Why it matters: Consumer (third-party beneficiary) enforcement; GPLv2 vs GPLv3 installation duties
case_law.Verification status: Verified (primary) for Dec. 2025 order; trial status secondary

case_law.Case: Artifex Software, Inc. v. Hancom, Inc.
case_law.Holding / status: Court accepted that GPL could be enforced as a contract as well as a license (dual-licensed Ghostscript)
case_law.Why it matters: Contract damages theory for GPL non-compliance

case_law.Holding / status: Orange held liable for GPLv2 violation (LASSO library) as copyright infringement; damages reported in the high six figures (EUR)
case_law.Why it matters: EU enforcement; large damages for GPL non-compliance

case_law.Court / citation: 9th Cir. No. 24-7700 (published opinion); N.D. Cal. No. 4:22-cv-06823
case_law.Holding / status: Affirmed dismissal of DMCA §1202(b) claim: Copilot/Codex outputs lacking CMI are new works, and §1202(b) requires removing or altering CMI from copies of existing works. "Identicality" is a misnomer - an evidentiary gloss, not an element; near-verbatim reproduction without CMI can support an inference of removal. "Input" (training-data) theory forfeited, not decided. Contract claims reported pending in district court
case_law.Why it matters: Narrows DMCA attribution claims against AI coding tools; retrieval-style systems may be treated differently; copyright and license claims unaffected

case_law.Holding / status: GPL issues raised by a downstream licensee in a commercial dispute; resolved without definitive GPL ruling
case_law.Why it matters: GPL as a counterclaim risk in commercial software disputes

regulatory.OSS-relevant rule: Exempts only technical documentation (53(1)(a)), downstream information (53(1)(b)) and the authorised-representative duty for non-EU providers. Requires a free and open-source license allowing access, use, modification and distribution without monetisation, plus public weights, architecture and usage information. Copyright policy and training-data summary duties still apply. No exemption for GPAI models with systemic risk.
regulatory.Diligence / compliance action: Do not assume an "open-weight" model qualifies: per Commission guidelines (July 18, 2025), scale-based restrictions and separate commercial licenses for certain uses are not "free and open-source."

regulatory.Key dates: In force Dec. 10, 2024; reporting obligations Sept. 11, 2026; full application Dec. 11, 2027; open-source steward reporting Dec. 11, 2027
regulatory.OSS-relevant rule: Manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents (24h early warning / 72h notification / final report). Creates "open-source software steward" role with lighter obligations
regulatory.Diligence / compliance action: Confirm whether target is a manufacturer or OSS steward; vulnerability handling process; SBOM; reporting readiness

regulatory.Instrument: OMB M-26-05 (Adopting a Risk-based Approach to Software and Hardware Security)
regulatory.OSS-relevant rule: Rescinds M-22-18 and M-23-16; Common Form attestation no longer required government-wide; agencies keep software/hardware inventories and may require SBOMs by contract
regulatory.Diligence / compliance action: Check each solicitation/contract for attestation or SBOM clauses
